text:
Alex W: Quick question — after the iterator RFC, what's the plan for making retries deterministic across Python async iterator, TS async generator, and Go channel? We keep hitting disagreement on whether resume token is opaque vs structured.
Maya P: my take: opaque token from server, SDK stores it as bytes/string, transport shouldn't peek. Keeps forward-compat and avoids per-language parsing.
Sam C: but if transport needs to do prefetch it may need a small nonce or lease. Can we add metadata header separate from token?
Alex W: idea: keep resume token opaque, add an optional 'continuation-hint' header that is purely for transport. Server sets it; SDK exposes it as `continuationHint` in response metadata and does not treat it as part of the cursor.
Jorge: :+1: I like that. TS/py can expose as `response.continuationHint` and not surface in page cursor. Go can include it on the iterator struct as an exported field.
Lena: Edge case — retries: if client retries a page fetch after a partial write, lease/hint needed for idempotency. Should we require servers to guarantee idempotent fetch(token)?
Sam C: yes. Server contract: fetch(token) must be idempotent. Lease is advisory; if server can't guarantee idempotency we fall back to sequential-only fetch with no aggressive prefetch.
Alex W: Implementation sketch:
```
// TS
for await (const item of client.listThings({pageSize: 100})) {
  // client handles resume tokens under the hood
}

// response object has metadata: { continuationHint?: string }
```
Maya P: For Python, async iterator will yield items and the iterator object will have `.resume_token` and `.continuation_hint` attributes (both optional strings). That lets advanced users checkpoint or rehydrate.
Jorge: On retries/backoff: transport should do a single socket-level retry that is transparent to SDK and let SDK handle higher-level idempotency/retry semantics. Avoid double-retries from both layers.
ci-bot: Deploy plan: canary server change + shim in SDKs to read continuation-hint header. Rolling deploy over 2 weeks; alert on increased 500s for list endpoints.
Lena: +1. Also let's document the server contract and add a unit test harness for server-side idempotency (failing servers should be flagged during onboarding).
Sam C: I'll own the SDK shims for TS and Python. Will add a small adapter in Go to carry the hint on the iterator.
Alex W: I'll own the server contract doc and a small compatibility test. Will post a draft link here in a bit. Also open question: semver for exposing continuationHint — technically a minor change but we should call it out in the changelog and SDK release notes.
Maya P: Follow-up: I'll benchmark prefetching with and without continuation hint for p50/p95/p99. If hint materially reduces tail latency we default prefetch-on for Dedicated customers.
Jorge: Sounds good. If no objections, we mark this RFC as "follow-up: token+hint" and close the design thread.
Alex W: No objections from me. :tada:
